title: Dispatch: Define campaign-rule domain model and precedence (attempt 1)
description:
Dispatch of eshyra-jhpt.1 (attempt 1). Spec and acceptance criteria live on eshyra-jhpt.1 and the epic eshyra-jhpt; read both. This bead carries the supervisor's pre-planning only.

WORKTREE / BRANCH
.worktrees/eshyra-jhpt.1.1 on branch eshyra-jhpt.1.1, cut from the integration branch eshyra-jhpt (which is at origin/main dded2d4). Work only inside that worktree.

MODEL CONFIG
gpt-5.6-luna, reasoning effort medium, YOLO dispatch via dispatch-codex.sh.

SCOPE OF THIS DISPATCH
Types, invariants, validation, precedence, and documentation only. NO SQLite schema, NO migration, NO storage APIs (that is eshyra-jhpt.2), NO prompt/context assembly (.3/.4), NO CLI (.5). Deliver a pure-domain module plus focused unit tests.

CODE SURVEY (verified against dded2d4)

1. A CONSUMER-SIDE CONTRACT ALREADY EXISTS ON MAIN AND IS BINDING.
   packages/core/src/discovery/types.ts already declares, and packages/core/src/discovery/campaignRuleSeam.ts already consumes:
     - CampaignRuleProjection { ruleIdentity, ruleKind: 'house-rule'|'ruling', status, origin, provenance, effectivePosition, supersededBy: string|null, scope, governingRecordKeys, ambiguityId?, oracleSupplied?, prose? }
     - CampaignRulingProjection extends it with ruleKind:'ruling', ambiguityId: string, selectedInterpretationId: string
     - CampaignRuleReadSeam { activeRulesAtPosition({campaignPosition?: string, candidateRecordKeys}), activeRulingsForAmbiguities(ambiguityIds) }
     - NULL_CAMPAIGN_RULE_SEAM
   These were built by the transition work (eshyra-o9bd.19.13 / W11) against the jhpt boundary. The eshyra-jhpt.1 domain model MUST be the authority these projections are derived from, and the projection shape must remain satisfiable without a discovery-local rule store. Do not fork a second, incompatible vocabulary. If the existing seam shape is genuinely wrong for the domain, say so in your completion notes and file a bd issue rather than silently diverging — the amendment path is a new child under eshyra-jhpt.
   Note ADR 0020 AMENDMENT A1 on eshyra-jhpt.3: the projection must carry the linked ambiguity ID and, where one exists, the governing pack record key. governingRecordKeys already exists on the seam type; make sure the domain model can produce it.

2. RulesAmbiguity (packages/core/src/rules/types.ts:100) is the pack-side counterpart:
     { id: 'ambiguity:<kebab>', question, source: [{locator, clauseId}], affects: string[], interpretations: [{id, summary}], canonicalResolution: null, runtimeDisposition: {status:'engine-pending', owner:'campaign-ruling'} }
   Validated by packages/core/src/rules/rulesAmbiguities.ts (optRulesAmbiguities), id regex /^ambiguity:[a-z0-9]+(?:-[a-z0-9]+)*$/. canonicalResolution is permanently null and owner is 'campaign-ruling' — that is precisely the hand-off this bead defines the receiving end of. A ruling's provenance references ambiguity.id and one of interpretations[].id; validation must reject an interpretation id that is not enumerated by that ambiguity (accept the ambiguity object or a lookup callback as an argument — do NOT copy pack data into the domain model).

3. CAMPAIGN POSITION HAS NO EXISTING MONOTONIC COUNTER. turn_trace is keyed (campaign_id, session_id, turn_id) and turnId is caller-supplied (orchestrator.ts input.turnId); only scene_log has a per-scene `seq` and campaign_arc a `sequence_no`. The discovery seam types campaignPosition as an opaque `string`. JUDGMENT CALL for you to make explicit and document: define CampaignPosition as a domain type with a canonical, deterministically ORDERABLE string encoding anchored on (sessionId, turnId) plus a monotonic ordinal, with parse/format/compare helpers and a total order. Deterministic ordering of the active set is an acceptance criterion in .1 and .3, so ordering must be a property of the domain model, not of a later SQL ORDER BY. eshyra-jhpt.2 will persist the ordinal; do not design something that requires a second store to compare two positions.

4. TEMPORAL MODES. The epic allows exactly two initial modes: ordinary prospective effectiveness, and effectiveness at the start of the immediately disputed turn (eshyra-jhpt.8 replay). Model this as a closed union; arbitrary historical retroactivity must fail validation. A disputed-turn effective position may only name the immediately preceding/current turn — the model should make an older-turn target representable-but-invalid so .8 can reject it with a domain error rather than inventing its own check.

5. IDIOMS TO FOLLOW.
   - Domain error class per module, e.g. `export class CampaignRuleError extends Error { constructor(message){super(message); this.name='CampaignRuleError';} }` — see campaign.ts:26, state/itemState.ts:147.
   - packages/core/src/validation.ts has requireNonEmpty; reuse rather than reinventing.
   - Placement: this is campaign-owned state, not pack semantics (ADR 0017). Put the module under packages/core/src/campaign/ (suggested `campaignRules.ts`) — NOT under src/rules/, which is pack territory. Tests under packages/core/test/.
   - EXPORT SURFACE: new core symbols default to `@eshyra/core/internal` (packages/core/src/internal.ts), not the root export. See AGENTS.md § Conventions. Do not add to index.ts.

6. WHAT PRECEDENCE MUST COVER. A documented, tested total ordering over: canonical pack semantics; unresolved RulesAmbiguity metadata (which resolves to "preserve uncertainty", never a default winner); active rulings; active house rules. Encode it as data/function with tests, not just prose. Non-goal guard: no prose-to-mechanics compilation anywhere.

REQUIRED OUTPUTS
- The domain module with types, closed unions, invariants, and a validate function that rejects every invalid combination named in the acceptance criteria (wrong kind/provenance pairing, ruling without ambiguity+interpretation linkage, interpretation not enumerated by the ambiguity, arbitrary retroactive effective position, supersession/revocation cycles or cross-campaign supersession, revoked-then-superseded contradictions).
- A pure function producing CampaignRuleProjection / CampaignRulingProjection from a domain rule, so .2/.3 and the existing discovery seam share one derivation.
- A precedence function with tests.
- Focused unit tests covering: ruling vs house-rule distinction, status/origin/effective-position/ordering/supersession/revocation, ambiguity linkage validity and invalidity, the two temporal modes and rejection of a third, deterministic total order over a shuffled set, and the documented non-goals.
- Documentation of the architecture decision and non-goals: a doc comment at the head of the module is required; add or extend a docs/ page only if you judge it genuinely needed.

VERIFICATION
`npm run verify:worktree` from the worktree root, BEFORE committing (it rewrites files).
